newsitem.title: UK: Celltech plunges on septic shock news.
newsitem.headline: Celltech plunges on septic shock news.

text.p: The value of UK biotech group Celltech Group Plc more than halved in pre-market trading on Wednesday after its German partner Bayer AG abandoned development of a leading drug for septic shock.

Shares in Celltech plunged 325 pence to 305 pence after the announcement by Bayer that BAYX-1351 did not show significant impact on mortality. The condition, which is a poisoning of the blood which can set in after surgery, kills up to 50 percent of patients affected.
The two companies had been making optimistic noises about the drug, which uses a mouse antibody developed by Bayer. The drug is the latest in a string of failed attempts to treat septic shock.
Although Celltech was not expected to gain huge profits from BAYX-1351, its success would have given the green light to development of a more important septic shock drug for Celltech, BAY-103356.
The company said it would now pursue development of this drug in Crohn's disease, a poorly treated inflammatory condition which mainly affects the small intestine.
Analysts had been attributing about two pounds of Celltech's value to the to septic shock products.
